title: Craft Beer 6-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday only)
drivers.evidence: Historical 14% sales drop on days after store closures; 6-day week vs 7-day reduces expected volume by ~14%.

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no event, no price change, and no promotion. The store closes Monday for renovation, reducing the selling days from 7 to 6. This is a known demand-lowering driver. Historical data shows a 14% drop in sales on the day after a store closure (1 week of 6-day sales vs 7-day), and the baseline already accounts for seasonality. The closure reduces expected sales by ~14%. No other drivers are present. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, which aligns with no promotion or event. The noise-adjusted effect of a closure is consistent with past observations.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 140.8 | 5%-95%: 62.7 - 228.6 | 10%-90%: 72.1 - 187.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-37% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
